content:
Maria Reyes: taking over primary for the next shift. handing off active incident in ap-southeast-1 (ap-sg1) — NIC flaps on a subset of GPU nodes causing server-side retries and p99 spikes for streaming chat sessions. page kicked off ~10m ago.

SRE Bot: incident created INC-APSG-2026-07 by pagerduty. alerts: srv-ap-sg1-nic-errors > 10m, streaming-p99-ap-sg1 > 300ms, packet-loss-ap-sg1 > 0.5%. current state: ongoing.

Dan Liu: context — started seeing small % of sessions with repeated reconnects (~0.8% of total). root appears correlated to NIC error counters (tx_drop/rx_err) on nodes in asg-gpu-apsg1-b. We cordoned two hosts and restarted the network driver on one host (ip link set dev eth0 down/up). errors reduced briefly then returned.

Kevin O'Connor: actions taken so far:
- routed ~80% of new streaming sessions to us-east-1 via routing policy to reduce customer impact (policy id: route-fallback-2026-03).
- cordoned problematic ASG instances: asg-gpu-apsg1-b-*.
- started provider ticket (GCP case 123456789) — provider acknowledges NIC firmware is being investigated.

Ashley Patel: customer impact summary for handoff:
- Impacted: customers on hosted region ap-southeast-1 for streaming/chat only (~6 customers reported degraded UX).
- Dedicated customers pinned to ap-sg1: two accounts (acct-omega, acct-cascade) seeing increased error/reconnects; outreach in progress by AMs.
- Non-impacted: embeddings, batch jobs unaffected.

SRE Bot: current metrics snapshot: streaming-p99-ap-sg1 = 620ms, streaming-error-rate = 1.1%, node-nic-err-count (rolling 15m) = 48.

Maria Reyes: ongoing mitigations / playbook pointers:
1) Keep routing weight shifted to fallback region until provider confirms fix. command: `POST /controlplane/routes` with body `{ "region": "us-east-1", "weight": 0.8 }` (ops-console).
2) Continue cordoning and draining suspicious hosts: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`.
3) If node flaps after uncordon, taint with `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule` and escalate to infra.
4) Run packet capture on one affected host and upload to incident bucket: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/apsg1-nic.pcap` then `gsutil cp /tmp/apsg1-nic.pcap gs://incidents/3187654321/`.

Dan Liu: note on rollback/restore: we disabled session-level retries client-side temporarily while we shifted routing to avoid duplicate charges and weird reconnect loops. if we re-enable retries, test with small canary traffic only.

Kevin O'Connor: gaps to call out during handoff:
- We do not yet have a firm ETA from provider — cloud-support-bot put case into hardware firmware queue.
- No automated customer notifications sent yet for dedicated customers; that'll be done by AMs ASAP.
- Observability: need to add NIC error counters to the main incident dashboard (I created temp panel but it's not in the saved board). link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ap-sg1-incident

SRE Bot: recent logs from one affected pod (truncated):
```
2026-03-15T03:24:10Z WARN stream_session: reconnect attempt=3 err=EOF
2026-03-15T03:24:12Z ERROR network: tx_drop=12 rx_err=4
2026-03-15T03:24:15Z INFO session: new_conn region=us-east-1
```

Ashley Patel: communications checklist for next steps:
- I will loop in AMs for acct-omega and acct-cascade and draft a brief incident note.
- Post an update to #customer-notify once we have provider ETA or if we decide to keep routing shift >30m.

Maria Reyes: immediate priorities for incoming primary/secondary:
- Primary (me): keep routing weight to fallback until provider confirms stabilized NIC stats for 30m. monitor p99 and error-rate.
- Secondary (Kevin): maintain cordon list and run packet captures on any newly flapping node; escalate to infra if a node goes into continuous NIC errors after restart.
- Ops contact: @infra-oncall (pager pinned).

Kevin O'Connor: I can take secondary now. noted. I'll keep a live list of cordoned node IDs under the incident doc and update every 10m.

Maria Reyes: runbook links and quick commands:
- runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ap-sg1-nic-flap (see sections: detection, network-driver-restart, routing-override)
- cordon helper: `scripts/cordon_and_drain.sh <node>` (in repo infra-tools)
- restore routing: `POST /controlplane/routes` body `{ "region": "ap-southeast-1", "weight": 1.0 }` and then monitor for 15m.

Dan Liu: anything to add — note that restarting the cni + driver on one host temporarily reduced errors for ~7 minutes before return. suggests either firmware-level issue or a network fabric problem at provider.

Maria Reyes: final — I'll be primary for next 4h window. Kevin is secondary. If you take over, please post in this thread with ack and current time. leaving this checklist as the single source of truth for this shift. :white_check_mark:

Kevin O'Connor: ack — taking secondary. will update at +10m. :thumbsup:

cloud-support-bot: GCP case 123456789 updated: provider has scheduled hardware-firmware review. next update window ~30-60m.

Maria Reyes: thanks. handoff complete.
